angleRead.name: Rachel Torres
angleRead.text: The table came in and Grand Lake is at the top again — eight incidents, down one from last cycle, but still the most in the city. I know that neighborhood. I know the corner where the calls stack up and the porch where the watch captain sits. What doesn't line up for me is the clearance rate — 21 percent. We answer the call, we get there in 10.6 minutes, and then what? Four out of five of those incidents don't close. That's not a response problem, that's a follow-through problem. Rockridge is slower on response — 11.8 minutes — and clears even less, 19 percent. So the two neighborhoods where people wait the longest and get the least back are the ones with the money and the ones with the lake

plan.focus: Grand Lake leads the city in incidents while clearance sits at 21% — what the public-safety command answers for when response times hold but cases don't close.
plan.why: The numbers show we get there fast enough but don't finish the work. That gap between response and clearance is where trust goes to die, and Grand Lake is the neighborhood carrying the heaviest load this cycle.

unverifiedLead: A neighborhood watch captain on Grand Avenue has been keeping a personal log of calls that never got follow-up visits — the count is not confirmed but the frustration is real.
A dispatcher mentioned that Grand Lake units are frequently pulled to cover gaps in adjacent districts, which may stretch response-to-clearance time — unconfirmed.
